at starte på.explanation: "At starte på" means "to start on" something, like a task: "Jeg starter på opgaven" (I start on the assignment). Without "på" (on), "at starte" (to start) is also used for engines and machines: "Bilen starter ikke" (The car won't start).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **starte på** et nyt projekt i dag.
sentence.en: I want to start on a new project today.

at stave.explanation: "At stave" means "to spell", saying the letters of a word one at a time. It is common when you give a name or an address on the phone: "Hvordan staver man det?" (How do you spell that?)

sentence.da: Kan du **stave** dit navn?
sentence.en: Can you spell your name?

at stege.explanation: "At stege" means "to fry" and "to roast": "Jeg steger kød i panden" (I fry meat in the pan) and "Vi steger en and i ovnen" (We roast a duck in the oven). Cooking in water is "at koge" (to boil).

forms.en: I have fried, I have roasted

sentence.da: Jeg skal **stege** æggene i panden.
sentence.en: I am going to fry the eggs in the pan.

at stemme.explanation: "At stemme" means "to vote": "Jeg stemmer på ham" (I vote for him). It also means "to be correct": "Det stemmer!" (That is right!)

sentence.da: Alle over atten år kan **stemme** ved valget.
sentence.en: Everyone over eighteen can vote in the election.

at stemme på.explanation: "At stemme på" means "to vote for" the person or party you choose. Danish uses "på" (on) where English says "for": "Vi stemte på Peter" (We voted for Peter).

sentence.da: Til valget vil jeg **stemme på** Anna.
sentence.en: At the election, I want to vote for Anna.

at stige.explanation: "At stige" means "to rise" and "to climb": "Prisen stiger" (The price is rising). "Han stiger op ad trappen" (He climbs up the stairs). With "ind" (in), it means to get into a vehicle: "Hun steg ind i bilen" (She got into the car).

sentence.da: Temperaturen kan **stige** til tredive grader.
sentence.en: The temperature can rise to thirty degrees.

at stige af.explanation: "At stige af" means "to get off", used for a bus, a train or a bike: "Hun stiger af cyklen" (She gets off the bike). The opposite is "at stige på" (to get on).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **stige af** bussen ved torvet.
sentence.en: I will get off the bus at the square.

at stige på.explanation: "At stige på" means "to get on", used for a bus, a train or a bike: "Vi stiger på toget i Odense" (We get on the train in Odense). The opposite is "at stige af" (to get off).

sentence.da: Vi må **stige på** bussen nu.
sentence.en: We have to get on the bus now.

at stikke.explanation: "At stikke" means "to sting" and "to stick": "Bien stak mig" (The bee stung me). It also means to put something in: "Jeg stikker pengene i lommen" (I stick the money in my pocket).

sentence.da: Du skal **stikke** nøglen i døren.
sentence.en: You have to stick the key in the door.

at stikke af.explanation: "At stikke af" means "to run off": you get away quickly, often from trouble. "Tyven stak af" (The thief ran off).

sentence.da: Drengen ville **stikke af**, men læreren så ham.
sentence.en: The boy wanted to run off, but the teacher saw him.

at stikke en finger i jorden.explanation: "At stikke en finger i jorden" means "to take stock", to stop and check where things really stand before you go on. Literally it is "to stick a finger in the ground", like feeling what the soil is like.

forms.da: Vi må stikke en finger i jorden
Hun stak en finger i jorden
Lad os stikke en finger i jorden

sentence.da: Vi må **stikke en finger i jorden** og se, hvor vi står.
sentence.en: We must take stock and see where we stand.

at stikke en kæp i hjulet.explanation: "At stikke en kæp i hjulet" means "to throw a wrench in the works", to spoil or block someone's plan, often on purpose. Literally, it means to stick a stick in the wheel. To name the person whose plan you spoil, add "for" (for): "stikke en kæp i hjulet for nogen" (to spoil things for someone).

forms.da: Han stikker en kæp i hjulet
forms.en: He throws a wrench in the works

forms.da: Hun stak en kæp i hjulet for os
Stik ikke en kæp i hjulet for dem
forms.en: Do not spoil things for them

sentence.da: Naboen vil **stikke en kæp i hjulet** for vores byggeplan.
sentence.en: The neighbor wants to throw a wrench in the works of our building plan.

at stille.explanation: "At stille" means "to put" or "to place" something upright: "Jeg stiller flasken på bordet" (I put the bottle on the table). For something lying flat, use "at lægge" (to lay): "Jeg lægger bogen på bordet" (I put the book on the table).

sentence.da: Kan du **stille** flasken på bordet?
sentence.en: Can you put the bottle on the table?

at stille et spørgsmål.explanation: "At stille et spørgsmål" means "to ask a question", literally "to put a question". With "at spørge" (to ask), you name the person you ask: "Jeg vil spørge dig om noget" (I want to ask you something).

sentence.da: Må jeg **stille et spørgsmål** om lektien?
sentence.en: May I ask a question about the homework?

at stille op.explanation: "At stille op" means "to run for office", to put your name forward in a vote: "Han stiller op for partiet" (He runs for the party). It also means to show up and play for a team: "Holdet stiller op til kampen" (The team turns out for the match). To line up, add "sig" (oneself): "Børnene stiller sig op i en række" (The children line up in a row).

sentence.da: Hun vil **stille op** til valget som borgmester.
sentence.en: She wants to run for mayor in the election.

at stille uret.explanation: "At stille uret" means "to set the clock". To say how much and which way, add an amount of time and a direction word: "stille uret en time frem" (set the clock an hour forward) or "stille uret en time tilbage" (set the clock an hour back).

sentence.da: Vi skal **stille uret** en time tilbage.
sentence.en: We have to set the clock back an hour.

at stimulere.explanation: "At stimulere" means "to stimulate", to wake up or support an activity or growth. It is also used for the economy: "at stimulere økonomien" (to boost the economy).

sentence.da: Leg kan **stimulere** børns fantasi og nysgerrighed.
sentence.en: Play can stimulate children's imagination and curiosity.

at stirre.explanation: "At stirre" means "to stare", to keep your eyes on something without turning away. To name the object you stare at, use "på" (at): "stirre på skærmen" (stare at the screen). Without "på", the verb means staring at nothing: "Han stirrer ud i luften" (He stares into space).

sentence.da: Det er uhøfligt at **stirre** på fremmede mennesker.
sentence.en: It is rude to stare at strangers.

at stjæle.explanation: "At stjæle" means "to steal", to take something that belongs to someone else. Robbing a bank or a person is different: "at røve" (to rob).

sentence.da: Man må ikke **stjæle** fra andre.
sentence.en: You must not steal from others.

at stole på.explanation: "At stole på" means "to trust", and "på" always stays with it: "Jeg stoler på min læge" (I trust my doctor). Even with "ikke" (not), "på" stays at the end: "Jeg stoler ikke på ham" (I do not trust him).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **stole på** min bedste ven.
sentence.en: I can trust my best friend.

at stoppe.explanation: "At stoppe" means "to stop". With "med" (with) it means "to quit doing something": "Jeg stopper med at spise slik" (I am going to stop eating candy).

sentence.da: Bilen skal **stoppe** ved det røde lys.
sentence.en: The car has to stop at the red light.

at straffe.explanation: "At straffe" means "to punish", to give someone a consequence for doing wrong. It also works for a mistake that costs you something: "Fejlen blev straffet med et mål" (The mistake was punished with a goal).

sentence.da: Dommeren kan **straffe** en spiller med et rødt kort.
sentence.en: The referee can punish a player with a red card.

at stramme.explanation: "At stramme" means "to tighten", to pull something until it sits firmly, like a screw or a strap. It is also used for rules: "at stramme reglerne" (to make the rules stricter).

sentence.da: Man kan **stramme** et bælte, når det sidder løst.
sentence.en: You can tighten a belt when it is loose.

at streame.explanation: "At streame" means "to stream", to watch or listen online without saving the file.

sentence.da: Vi vil **streame** en film i aften.
sentence.en: We want to stream a movie tonight.

at strejke.explanation: "At strejke" means "to strike", to stop work together to demand better conditions: "Lærerne strejker" (The teachers are on strike). It is something a group does together, not one person alone.

sentence.da: Lærerne vil **strejke**, fordi de ønsker højere løn.
sentence.en: The teachers want to strike because they want higher pay.

at strikke.explanation: "At strikke" means "to knit", making fabric from yarn with two needles. Crocheting is a different word: "at hækle" (to crochet).

sentence.da: Min mormor kan **strikke** en varm trøje.
sentence.en: My grandmother can knit a warm sweater.

at stryge.explanation: "At stryge" means "to iron" clothes. It also means "to stroke" something gently: "Hun stryger katten" (She strokes the cat).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **stryge** en skjorte før mødet.
sentence.en: I have to iron a shirt before the meeting.

at stræbe.explanation: "At stræbe" means "to strive", to work hard over a long time toward a goal you want. To name that goal, use "efter" (for): "stræbe efter succes" (to strive for success). "Stræbsom" (ambitious) is the same word family.

sentence.da: Han vil **stræbe** efter at blive den bedste i klassen.
sentence.en: He wants to strive to become the best in the class.

at strække.explanation: "At strække" means "to stretch" something out, like your arms or a rope. To stretch your own body, add "sig" (oneself): "Katten strækker sig" (The cat stretches).

sentence.da: Det er vigtigt at **strække** benene efter løbeturen.
sentence.en: It is important to stretch your legs after the run.

at strække sig.explanation: "At strække sig" means "to stretch" your own body: "Han strækker sig efter træning" (He stretches after exercise). The word "sig" changes with who stretches: "jeg strækker mig" (I stretch), "vi strækker os" (we stretch).

sentence.da: Katten vil **strække sig** i solen.
sentence.en: The cat wants to stretch in the sun.

at strø.explanation: "At strø" means "to sprinkle", to scatter small bits over a surface, like sugar or sand. It is also used for scattering things around: "strø om sig med penge" (to throw money around).

sentence.da: Vi må **strø** sand foran døren, når der er is.
sentence.en: We must sprinkle sand in front of the door when there is ice.

at studere.explanation: "At studere" means "to study", especially at a university. For studying at home for a test, Danes often say "at læse til en eksamen" (to study for an exam; literally, "to read for an exam").

related.en: a study, a course of study

sentence.da: Hun vil **studere** medicin på universitetet.
sentence.en: She wants to study medicine at the university.

at styre.explanation: "At styre" means "to steer" and "to control", like steering a car or a boat. It also means "to run" something: "Han styrer firmaet" (He runs the company).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **styre** båden selv.
sentence.en: I can steer the boat myself.

at styrke.explanation: "At styrke" means "to strengthen", to make something stronger or better able to resist. It also fits relationships: "Turen styrkede venskabet" (The trip strengthened the friendship).

sentence.da: Daglig motion kan **styrke** hjertet og musklerne.
sentence.en: Daily exercise can strengthen the heart and the muscles.

at styrte.explanation: "At styrte" means "to rush" and "to crash", both a fast movement that is hard to control. Without "ned" (down), it is about speed: "Jeg styrtede hjem" (I rushed home). With "ned", it means falling or crashing down: "Flyet styrtede ned" (The plane crashed).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **styrte** ud af døren, når klokken ringer.
sentence.en: The children will rush out the door when the bell rings.

at stå.explanation: "At stå" means "to stand". Danish also uses it for things that are placed upright, such as "Flasken står på bordet" (The bottle is on the table), and for text written somewhere: "Der står et navn på døren" (There is a name on the door).

sentence.da: Man kan **stå** eller sidde i bussen.
sentence.en: You can stand or sit on the bus.

at stå af.explanation: "At stå af" means "to get off", used for a bus, a train or the metro. For a bike or a horse, use "at stige af" (to get off).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **stå af** ved næste stop.
sentence.en: I will get off at the next stop.

at stå for.explanation: "At stå for" means "to be in charge of" a job or a task: "Jeg står for maden" (I am in charge of the food).

forms.en: I have been in charge of

sentence.da: Min bror vil **stå for** maden til festen.
sentence.en: My brother will be in charge of the food for the party.

at stå i kø.explanation: "At stå i kø" means "to stand in line". "Kø" (line) also works for cars in a traffic jam: "Der er kø på motorvejen" (There is a traffic jam on the highway).

sentence.da: Vi må **stå i kø** for billetter.
sentence.en: We have to stand in line for tickets.

at stå op.explanation: "At stå op" means "to get up" out of bed, literally to stand up. When saying what you have done, Danish uses "er" (am) instead of "har" (have): "Jeg er stået op" (I have gotten up). To stand up from a chair, Danes say "at rejse sig" (to stand up).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **stå op** klokken syv.
sentence.en: I want to get up at seven.

at stå på ski.explanation: "At stå på ski" means "to ski", literally to stand on skis. Water skiing works the same way: "at stå på vandski" (to water ski).

sentence.da: Vi vil **stå på ski** i Norge.
sentence.en: We want to ski in Norway.

at støde på.explanation: "At støde på" means "to come across", to see or notice something by chance, without looking for it. It also works for difficulties: "støde på modstand" (face resistance).

sentence.da: Vi kan **støde på** problemer, når vi bygger huset.
sentence.en: We may come across problems when we build the house.

at stønne.explanation: "At stønne" means "to groan", to make a deep sound from pain, effort or annoyance. To name the cause of the groan, use "over" (about): "stønne over varmen" (to groan about the heat).

sentence.da: Man kan **stønne**, når man løfter noget meget tungt.
sentence.en: You can groan when you lift something very heavy.

at støtte.explanation: "At støtte" means "to support" a person or a cause. It also means "to lean on": "Han støttede sig til væggen" (He leaned on the wall).

sentence.da: Jeg vil altid **støtte** dig.
sentence.en: I will always support you.

at støve af.explanation: "At støve af" means "to dust", to wipe dust off furniture and things. "Af" (off) comes last: "Jeg støver hylderne af" (I dust the shelves). It also fits old skills: "støve sit fransk af" (dust off your French).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **støve af** i stuen, når gæsterne kommer.
sentence.en: I will dust in the living room when the guests come.

at støvsuge.explanation: "At støvsuge" means "to vacuum" a floor or a rug. It is built from støv (dust) and suge (suck), and the machine is "en støvsuger" (a vacuum cleaner).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **støvsuge** stuen i dag.
sentence.en: I have to vacuum the living room today.

at suge.explanation: "At suge" means "to suck", pulling something in with your mouth or a machine. To name the object you suck on, use "på" (on): "Babyen suger på sutten" (The baby sucks on the pacifier).

sentence.da: Barnet kan **suge** saften op med et sugerør.
sentence.en: The child can suck the juice up with a straw.

at sukke.explanation: "At sukke" means "to sigh", letting out a deep breath when you are tired, sad or annoyed. The noun is "et suk" (a sigh).

sentence.da: Min bror kan **sukke** højt, når han keder sig.
sentence.en: My brother can sigh loudly when he is bored.

at sulte.explanation: "At sulte" means "to starve", to suffer from having too little food. To say you are simply hungry, use "Jeg er sulten" (I am hungry), not "sulte".

sentence.da: Ingen skal **sulte**, når der er mad nok til alle.
sentence.en: Nobody should starve when there is enough food for everyone.

at summe.explanation: "At summe" means "to buzz", to make the soft, steady sound of a bee, a fly or a machine. A place can buzz too: "Byen summer af liv" (The city buzzes with life). To hum a tune, use "at nynne" (to hum), not "summe".

sentence.da: Om sommeren kan man høre fluer **summe** i vinduet.
sentence.en: In summer you can hear flies buzz in the window.

at supplere.explanation: "At supplere" means "to supplement", to add something to what you already have so that it is enough. With "hinanden" (each other), it means they fill in what the other lacks: "De supplerer hinanden" (They complement each other).

sentence.da: Du kan **supplere** din kost med frugt og grønt.
sentence.en: You can supplement your diet with fruit and vegetables.

at sutte.explanation: "At sutte" means "to suck", to take something into the mouth and keep it there. Danish says "på" (on): "Babyen sutter på flasken" (The baby sucks on the bottle).

sentence.da: Barnet kan lide at **sutte** på tommelfingeren.
sentence.en: The child likes to suck on the thumb.

at svare.explanation: "At svare" means "to answer" or "to reply". To answer a question, add "på" (on): "svare på et spørgsmål" (to answer a question).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **svare** på spørgsmålet.
sentence.en: I can answer the question.

at svare igen.explanation: "At svare igen" means "to talk back", to reply to someone in a rude or cheeky way, usually a child to a parent or teacher: "Svar ikke igen!" (Do not talk back!) "Igen" usually means "again", but here it means "back".

sentence.da: Drengen må ikke **svare igen**, når mor skælder ud.
sentence.en: The boy must not talk back when mom scolds him.

at svare på.explanation: "At svare på" means "to answer" or "to reply to", and "på" (on) always stays with it: "Jeg svarer på din besked" (I reply to your message).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **svare på** din mail i morgen.
sentence.en: I will reply to your email tomorrow.

at svede.explanation: "At svede" means "to sweat", from heat or effort. It also fits nerves: "Hun sveder over eksamen" (She is sweating over the exam).

sentence.da: Når det er varmt, kan jeg **svede** meget.
sentence.en: When it is hot, I can sweat a lot.

at svigte.explanation: "At svigte" means "to let down" or "to fail", to go back on someone who trusted you. It also describes things that stop working when needed: "Bremserne svigtede" (The brakes failed).

sentence.da: En ven må aldrig **svigte** en anden, når det går galt.
sentence.en: A friend must never let another down when things go wrong.

at svinge.explanation: "At svinge" means "to swing", to move back and forth or in an arc, like a pendulum. It also means to turn while driving or biking: "Jeg svinger til højre" (I turn right).

sentence.da: Du skal **svinge** til venstre ved lyskrydset.
sentence.en: You must turn left at the traffic light.

at svække.explanation: "At svække" means "to weaken", to make something less strong, often little by little.

sentence.da: Lange nætter uden søvn kan **svække** kroppen.
sentence.en: Long nights without sleep can weaken the body.

at sværge.explanation: "At sværge" means "to swear", to promise something very seriously, for example in court. It is not the word for bad language. For that, Danes use "at bande" (to curse).

sentence.da: Vidnet skal **sværge** at sige sandheden i retten.
sentence.en: The witness must swear to tell the truth in court.

at svømme.explanation: "At svømme" means "to swim". For a quick dip, Danes also say "at bade" (to go for a swim): "Vi bader i søen" (We are going for a swim in the lake).

sentence.da: Fisk kan **svømme** i vandet.
sentence.en: Fish can swim in the water.

at sy.explanation: "At sy" means "to sew", joining cloth with a needle and thread. It also covers closing a cut with stitches: "Lægen syede såret" (The doctor stitched the wound).

sentence.da: Min mor kan **sy** sine egne kjoler.
sentence.en: My mother can sew her own dresses.

at sygemelde sig.explanation: "At sygemelde sig" means "to call in sick", telling your employer that you are ill.

sentence.da: Hun må **sygemelde sig**, fordi hun har feber.
sentence.en: She has to call in sick because she has a fever.

at symbolisere.explanation: "At symbolisere" means "to symbolize", to stand for an idea or feeling. The symbol comes first, then the idea: "Duen symboliserer fred" (The dove symbolizes peace), not the other way around.

sentence.da: Et rødt hjerte kan **symbolisere** kærlighed.
sentence.en: A red heart can symbolize love.

at synes.explanation: "At synes" means "to think", in the sense of having an opinion: "Jeg synes, det er godt" (I think it is good). For a guess about a fact, use "at tro" (to believe, to guess): "Jeg tror, han kommer" (I think he is coming). "Hvad synes du?" (What do you think?)

sentence.da: Hvad **synes** du om maden?
sentence.en: What do you think about the food?

at synge.explanation: "At synge" means "to sing". To sing along with others or with a recording, add "med" (with): "Jeg synger med" (I sing along).

sentence.da: Hun kan **synge** en smuk sang.
sentence.en: She can sing a beautiful song.

at synke.explanation: "At synke" means "to sink" and also "to swallow". For a ship or a stone: "Skibet synker" (The ship sinks). For food or a pill: "Jeg kan ikke synke tabletten" (I cannot swallow the pill).

sentence.da: Den tunge sten vil **synke** i vandet.
sentence.en: The heavy stone will sink in the water.

at såre.explanation: "At såre" means "to hurt" or "to wound", mostly someone's feelings. For pain in the body, Danes say "at gøre ondt" (to hurt): "Det gør ondt" (It hurts).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **såre** dig, men jeg må sige sandheden.
sentence.en: I do not want to hurt you, but I must tell the truth.

at sælge.explanation: "At sælge" means "to sell". "Til salg" (for sale) is used on a sign: "Bilen er til salg" (The car is for sale).

sentence.da: Bageren vil **sælge** brød i butikken.
sentence.en: The baker wants to sell bread in the store.

at sænke.explanation: "At sænke" means "to lower", and also "to sink" something on purpose: "at sænke stemmen" (to lower your voice), "Piraterne sænker skibet" (The pirates sink the ship). When something goes down by itself, use "at synke" (to sink): "Skibet synker" (The ship sinks).

sentence.da: Butikken vil **sænke** priserne, fordi der er for få kunder.
sentence.en: The store wants to lower the prices because there are too few customers.

at sætte.explanation: "At sætte" means "to put" or "to place" something somewhere: "Jeg sætter bogen på hylden" (I put the book on the shelf). Do not mix it up with "at sidde" (to sit), which describes where you already are. "Sæt dig" (Sit down) uses "sætte" too.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sætte** koppen på bordet.
sentence.en: I want to put the cup on the table.

at sætte i gang.explanation: "At sætte i gang" means "to start" or "to launch", to get something running: "Vi sætter projektet i gang" (We are launching the project). When the thing starts by itself, use "at komme i gang" (to get going): "Projektet kommer i gang" (The project gets going).

sentence.da: Når I er klar, vil jeg **sætte i gang**.
sentence.en: When you are ready, I will get things started.

at sætte ind.explanation: "At sætte ind" means "to put in", and also "to deposit": "Jeg sætter pengene ind på kontoen" (I put the money into the account). It can mean "to put into service": "Vi sætter flere busser ind" (We are putting more buses into service).

sentence.da: Jeg går i banken for at **sætte ind**.
sentence.en: I am going to the bank to make a deposit.

at sætte pris på.explanation: "At sætte pris på" means "to appreciate", to value what someone does or gives. Add "stor" (big) for more: "Jeg sætter stor pris på det" (I really appreciate it).

sentence.da: Man skal **sætte pris på** sine venner.
sentence.en: You should appreciate your friends.

at sætte på.explanation: "At sætte på" means "to put on" something that is turned on or heated, such as music, a pot of coffee or the stove. For clothes, use "at tage tøj på" (to put on clothes).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sætte på** noget kaffe, før gæsterne kommer.
sentence.en: I will put on some coffee before the guests come.

at sætte sig.explanation: "At sætte sig" means "to sit down": "Jeg sætter mig i sofaen" (I sit down on the sofa). To say you are already sitting, use "at sidde" (to sit): "Jeg sidder i sofaen" (I am sitting on the sofa).

sentence.da: Han vil **sætte sig** på stolen.
sentence.en: He wants to sit down on the chair.

at søge.explanation: "At søge" means "to apply" and "to search": "Jeg søger et job" (I am applying for a job). To search for a thing, add "efter" (for): "Jeg søger efter mine nøgler" (I am searching for my keys).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **søge** et nyt job i København.
sentence.en: I want to apply for a new job in Copenhagen.

at søge efter.explanation: "At søge efter" means "to search for" something you want to find. Without "efter" (for), "at søge" is used to apply: "Hun søger et job" (She is applying for a job).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **søge efter** en billig lejlighed.
sentence.en: I want to search for a cheap apartment.

at søge ind på.explanation: "At søge ind på" means "to apply to" a school or a study program. To apply for a job, say "at søge et job" (to apply for a job).

sentence.da: Min søster vil **søge ind på** universitetet i år.
sentence.en: My sister wants to apply to the university this year.

at søge job.explanation: "At søge job" means "to apply for a job", and also "to look for work": "Jeg søger job som lærer" (I am looking for a job as a teacher). For one specific position, say "at søge en stilling" (to apply for a position).

forms.en: I have applied for a job

sentence.da: Jeg vil **søge job** i en bank.
sentence.en: I want to apply for a job at a bank.

at søge om.explanation: "At søge om" means "to apply for", when you ask for something official: "søge om tilladelse" (apply for a permit), "søge om støtte" (apply for support). For a job, say "at søge" (to apply): "søge et job" (apply for a job).

sentence.da: Han skal **søge om** et visum i dag.
sentence.en: He has to apply for a visa today.

at sørge for.explanation: "At sørge for" means "to take care of" something: "Jeg sørger for maden" (I take care of the food). It also means "to make sure": "Sørg for at låse døren" (Make sure you lock the door).

forms.en: to make sure / take care of
I make sure / take care of
I made sure / took care of
I have made sure / taken care of

sentence.da: Jeg skal **sørge for** børnene i aften.
sentence.en: I'll take care of the children tonight.

en sadel.explanation: "En sadel" means "a saddle", the seat on a horse's back, held in place by a strap under its belly. A bike seat is called "en sadel" too.

sentence.da: Rytteren sidder i en **sadel** på hestens ryg.
sentence.en: The rider sits in a saddle on the horse's back.

en sag.explanation: "En sag" means "a matter" or "a case". For a topic, it is "a matter": "Det er en anden sag" (That is a different matter). At work or in court, it is "a case": "Advokaten arbejder på en sag" (The lawyer is working on a case).

sentence.da: Politiet arbejder på en vigtig **sag**.
sentence.en: The police are working on an important case.

en sagsbehandler.explanation: "En sagsbehandler" means "a caseworker", a public employee who looks into your situation and decides on things like benefits or support. It is built from sag (case) and behandler (someone who handles).

sentence.da: Min **sagsbehandler** ringer, når hun har læst min ansøgning.
sentence.en: My caseworker will call when she has read my application.

en saks.explanation: "En saks" means "a pair of scissors". Danes say "en saks" where English says "a pair of scissors": "Kan jeg låne din saks?" (Can I borrow your scissors?)

sentence.da: Jeg klipper papir med en **saks**.
sentence.en: I cut paper with a pair of scissors.

en sal.explanation: "En sal" means "a hall", a big space for meetings, parties or shows. It is not a hallway; that is "en gang" (a hallway).

sentence.da: Koncerten foregår i den store **sal**.
sentence.en: The concert takes place in the big hall.

en salamander.explanation: "En salamander" means "a salamander", a small animal with a long tail that looks like a lizard but has smooth, moist skin instead of scales.

sentence.da: Man finder ofte en **salamander** under en sten ved vandet.
sentence.en: You often find a salamander under a rock by the water.

en salat.explanation: "En salat" means "a salad" and also "lettuce". You can tell which one it is from the context of the sentence: "Jeg spiser en salat til frokost" (I eat a salad for lunch), but "en hovedsalat" (a head of lettuce) is the plant.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **salat** med tomat og agurk.
sentence.en: I eat a salad with tomato and cucumber.

en saltbøsse.explanation: "En saltbøsse" means "a salt shaker", the small container you shake salt from at the table. It is built from salt (salt) and bøsse (a small can).

sentence.da: Jeg ryster salt på maden fra en **saltbøsse**.
sentence.en: I shake salt onto the food from a salt shaker.

en salve.explanation: "En salve" means "an ointment", a thick treatment you rub on the skin, such as for a rash or a sore muscle. The same word also means a volley: "en salve skud" (a volley of shots).

sentence.da: Lægen gav mig en **salve** til mit udslæt.
sentence.en: The doctor gave me an ointment for my rash.

en samlever.explanation: "En samlever" means "a live-in partner", someone you live with as a couple, even if you are not married. The word comes from sammen (together) and at leve (to live).

sentence.da: Min **samlever** og jeg bor sammen, men vi er ikke gift.
sentence.en: My partner and I live together, but we are not married.

en samling.explanation: "En samling" means "a collection", many things of one kind that you keep together, like stamps or books. In a kindergarten, "samling" is also the circle time when all the children gather.

sentence.da: Min onkel har en stor **samling** af gamle mønter.
sentence.en: My uncle has a big collection of old coins.

en sammenhæng.explanation: "En sammenhæng" means "a connection", the way two things belong together. It also means context: "i den sammenhæng" (in that context).

sentence.da: Der er en **sammenhæng** mellem rygning og lungesygdom.
sentence.en: There is a link between smoking and lung disease.

en sammenkomst.explanation: "En sammenkomst" means "a get-together", a small gathering where people meet to talk, like a family afternoon or a work birthday. It is quieter than "en fest" (a party), often just talk and something to drink.

sentence.da: Vi drak kaffe og spiste kage til en **sammenkomst** hos mormor.
sentence.en: We drank coffee and ate cake at a get-together at Grandma's.

en sammenligning.explanation: "En sammenligning" means "a comparison", looking at two things to see how they are alike or different. It is often used with "mellem" (between): "en sammenligning mellem to byer" (a comparison between two cities).

sentence.da: I **sammenligning** med Sverige er Danmark et lille land.
sentence.en: In comparison with Sweden, Denmark is a small country.

en sammensværgelse.explanation: "En sammensværgelse" means "a conspiracy", a plan made in hiding by a group of people to do something illegal or harmful, such as overthrowing a ruler.

sentence.da: Politiet afslørede en **sammensværgelse** mod kongen.
sentence.en: The police uncovered a conspiracy against the king.

en samtale.explanation: "En samtale" means "a conversation". It is built from sam- (together) and tale (talk). With "telefon" (phone) in front, it is a phone call: "en telefonsamtale" (a phone call).

sentence.da: To mennesker har en **samtale**, når de taler sammen.
sentence.en: Two people have a conversation when they talk together.

en samtaleøvelse.explanation: "En samtaleøvelse" means "a conversation exercise", an exercise where learners talk to each other, often in pairs, to practice speaking. It is built from samtale (conversation) and øvelse (practice).

sentence.da: I en **samtaleøvelse** taler vi sammen to og to.
sentence.en: In a conversation exercise, we talk together in pairs.

en samvittighed.explanation: "En samvittighed" means "a conscience", the inner voice that tells you whether something you did is right or wrong. A clear one is "en ren samvittighed" (a clear conscience).

sentence.da: Hun fik dårlig **samvittighed** efter løgnen.
sentence.en: She got a guilty conscience after the lie.
